top_strength: The discovery in the first half was genuinely strong and the box question was textbook. Rather than asking a customer standing in an unpacked apartment to guess a number, he gave her the benchmark first — 'we'll typically see anywhere from fifteen to 25 boxes in a one bedroom' — then handed her the outlier test: 'a lot of kitchen wear, a book collection, a lot of small knick-knacks... do you think you would come outside that range?' He also worked the destination properly, chasing down the storage address by name when she did not have it, then confirming first floor, indoor, and unit size. The best judgment call was on assembly: he explained unprompted that he would have quoted longer for an apartment-to-apartment move but storage is 'pretty stop and drop,' which shows he understands what actually drives the hours. And the rapport was real — sharing that he had moved his own stuff a month ago and 'it is absolutely miserable' opened Nicole up completely, and she volunteered that she would use Einstein again for her house purchase.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: you had the booking and you let it walk. Nicole said 'I'm definitely okay with the price' — that is as clear a buying signal as we get — and the answer was 'whenever you are ready.' Say this instead: 'Nicole, that's great to hear. I've got the fifteenth open right now, and since we don't require a deposit and there's no cancellation fee, let's go ahead and lock it in — you can move the date any time as long as the spot's open. Want me to get that on the schedule?' There is zero risk to her and it converts a maybe into a booked job. Second priority: No Worries never came up, and she flagged glass four separate times. That is the exact anxiety this differentiator exists to answer — 'the state minimum is sixty cents per pound, which honestly doesn't cover anything, so we set aside two thousand dollars per move to repair, replace, or reimburse, and we handle it in two or three business days.' Third: she told you she is overwhelmed packing three years of stuff and you never offered packing service or an Ecobox referral. Both would have helped her and grown the job. Fourth: your prep speech was one reactive sentence. Build it out — consolidation examples, the carload tip, and 'does that make sense?' — especially with a customer who already wants to do some of the hauling herself. Last thing: watch the filler. 'Yeah, we get it' landed five or six times where naming what she actually said would have hit harder.
phone_presence_notes: Genuine rapport carried this call — the self-disclosure about his own miserable move landed, Nicole opened up about her sister and her house plans and volunteered that she would use Einstein again, which is a strong satisfaction signal; held back from a 5 by the repeated mechanical 'yeah, we get it' filler and no use of her name until the closing line.
